## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — regression test

data.title: Fix: drive stranded-child commit evidence matches the work-item id in a commit body, producing a false stranded verdict

## Objective

Make `/skill:ship release` judge the importance of the work items in the release and propose the semantically correct semver bump (patch, minor, or major), instead of always bumping patch — with the producer asked in the PI session before any non-patch bump is applied.

## Problem Statement

The ship skill currently always increments the `z` (patch) component of the release version (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` defaults `BUMP="patch"`), even when the release adds new or breaking capability. Releases that add features therefore ship as patch versions (e.g. `v0.1.19` instead of `v0.2.0`), misrepresenting the release's impact and forcing the producer to remember `--bump minor` manually.

## Users

- **Release manager (the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`)** — must judge the release's importance from the items being shipped and propose the right bump without extra flags.
- **Producer** — must see and approve any non-patch bump, in the session, with a full justification naming the items that triggered it.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when every item in the release is a fix, chore, or documentation change, I want the release to bump patch automatically so that I don't have to think about semver.
- As a release manager, when the release contains meaningful new capability, I want to propose a minor bump with evidence, rather than silently shipping it as a patch.
- As a producer, I want to be asked, in the session, before a minor or major bump is applied, with a justification naming the items and why they warrant the bump — and I want to be able to decline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- The agent judges the importance of the release from those items and proposes exactly one bump: **patch** when the release only fixes, documents, or maintains; **minor** when it adds meaningful new capability; **major** when it breaks or removes existing capability or otherwise changes behaviour incompatibly (the existing `--bump` override remains available).
- A **patch** proposal proceeds automatically with no producer interaction — the current `--bump patch` behaviour and `merge-dev-to-main.sh` default are unchanged.
- A **minor or major** proposal prints a full justification — each contributing item ID and title, why it warrants the bump, and the proposed `old → new` version — and the agent asks the producer **in the PI session**; no git mutation, tag, PR, or worklog close occurs until the producer approves.
- Producer approval proceeds with the approved `--bump`; a declined non-patch proposal is honoured (the agent does not apply it, and records the decision and the producer's preferred bump in the session and on the release's work item).
- In a non-interactive/headless context where the producer cannot be asked, a minor or major proposal is never auto-approved: the agent records the justification, flags the item for producer review, and stops.
- The judgement is based on the release items' content (Impact/description/capability), not on `issueType` or a label lookup; the justification cites the evidence used.
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics rather than duplicating version arithmetic.
- Unit tests cover: candidate gathering (including an empty candidate set), the review packet/justification rendering, patch auto-proceed, and the non-patch approval-pending behaviour (no mutation); no test reads or mutates the live worklog.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, and code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Releases that add or break capability will carry a version number that reflects it, and producers will be asked in-session to approve that call with evidence instead of policing `--bump` flags by hand.

## Existing State

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` sets `BUMP="patch"` by default and accepts `--bump patch|minor|major` (already validates the value).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` parses and forwards `--bump` to the merge script; the wrapper has no bump evaluation step and its documented exit codes are `0`–`14`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` already implements `patch`/`minor`/`major` arithmetic correctly (including `z = 0` on minor and `y = z = 0` on major) and resolves `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` as the version source.
- Release candidates are items with `stage: in_review` (`check-audit-gate.js::getCandidateItems`), so the candidate set already exists.
- The release wrapper subprocess is non-interactive, but the ship skill itself is a PI skill executed by an agent in a session — the agent, not the shell script, is the component that can ask the producer.

## Desired Change

1. Add a small, unit-testable helper (e.g. `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js`) that gathers release candidates and renders a compact review packet: per item `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, `## Impact` (or user story) and a truncated description excerpt, plus the current version and the three candidate bump outcomes. It gathers and renders only — no judgement, no mutation.
2. Add a "Version bump evaluation" step at the start of the documented release workflow in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (before gates and merge): run the preflight, judge the release's importance, and choose patch/minor/major.
3. Patch → run the release normally (patch is the existing default).
4. Minor/major → present the justification to the producer in the session and wait for approval; on approval run `run-release.js --bump <approved>`; on decline, do not apply.
5. Keep the judgement rationale and the producer's decision in the session output and, where the release is tied to a work item, in a comment so the version choice is auditable.
6. Update `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the SKILL.md workflow/argument docs to describe the evaluation step and the in-session approval gate.

## Constraints

- **Judgement stays with the agent:** no issue-type or label mapping, and no mechanical classifier is added — the evaluation prompt/rubric is documented, and the agent makes the call from the items' content.
- **Producer gates non-patch bumps:** minor and major bumps must never be applied without an explicit producer approval in the session. Patch bumps stay automatic.
- **Fail-closed in headless runs:** where no producer is available (downtime/automated dispatches), a minor/major proposal must stop with producer review rather than self-approve.
- **Backward compatible:** an explicit `--bump` keeps its current meaning and precedence; invoking `merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly keeps its `patch` default.
- **No duplicated version arithmetic:** reuse `bump-version.js` for the actual bump; the new code only gathers evidence and renders the proposal.
- **Fail-safe:** an unreadable/empty candidate set must default to patch with a warning and must never block a release that would otherwise succeed; a preflight failure must not mutate the repository.
- **No live-worklog test access:** unit tests must inject the candidate-fetch boundary.
- **Auditability:** the proposed and approved bump, the justification, and the producer's decision are recorded (session output plus a work-item comment for item-linked releases).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — new "Version bump evaluation" workflow step, in-session approval gate, argument/behaviour docs.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` — new candidate-gathering/review-packet helper (and its tests).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — unchanged `--bump` forwarding, plus any logging of the decided bump; verify no new git side effects.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — receives the decided `--bump`; default unchanged.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — reused as-is for arithmetic (verify minor resets patch to `0`, major resets minor and patch).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems` is the release-candidate source.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — reference for the evaluation step and approval gate.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new unit tests for the preflight helper and the approval-pending path.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** — Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (introduced the bump step and `v<semver>` tag convention).
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** — ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (version source resolution).
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** — Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs.
- **SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL** — bump-version.js isMainModule check fails on symlinked install paths.
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** — Close work items when shipping (uses the released version in `Shipped in v<version>` markers).
- **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** — Newly-created-tag gate (precedent for a fail-closed startup gate with a distinct exit code).
- **SA-0MUIVIJFT0009ZNV** — Missing-script fail-fast (precedent for refusing early, before any git/worklog side effects).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Judgement subjectivity (risk):** "meaningful new capability" is a judgement call, and two agents could judge the same release differently. Mitigation: a documented rubric (new capability → minor, breaking change → major, fixes/docs/maintenance only → patch), the evidence-based justification, and the producer's in-session approval for every non-patch bump.
- **Producer availability (risk):** a headless release cannot ask anyone. Mitigation: a non-patch proposal in a headless run stops with producer review instead of self-approving; patch releases are unaffected.
- **Agent discipline (risk):** the gate lives in the documented workflow, so a release run by bypassing the skill (direct `run-release.js`) is not gated. Mitigation: document the workflow as the canonical path, and keep the version arithmetic and safety gates in the script unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-item bump annotations, automatic CHANGELOG grouping, and mechanical classification are separate opportunities and should be filed as follow-up items rather than folded into this change.
- **Empty candidate set:** a release with no `in_review` items (e.g. hotfix) defaults to patch and logs why.
- **`--skip-checks` interaction (assumption):** `--skip-checks` bypasses branch/critical gates only; the bump evaluation still runs, and an explicit `--bump` remains an operator override.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (basis for minor-worthiness):** How should the release's importance be judged?
  - Options considered: (A) by `issueType`; (B) by `priority`; (C) by an explicit label/tag; (D) the agent's interpretation of the items' importance.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's not about issue type or label. It's about your interpretation of the importance of the items in the release. Make the best call you can. Check with the producer." → **Option D**, with a documented rubric and producer confirmation.
- **Q2 (approval mechanism):** How is the producer asked to approve a proposed minor/major bump?
  - Options considered: (A) fail-closed exit code + producer re-runs with `--bump`; (B) an interactive prompt inside the PI session; (C) automatic bump with a warning.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's a skill in PI, ask in the session." → **Option B**: the agent presents the justification and asks the producer in the session; the subprocess itself stays non-interactive.
- **Q3 (major inference):** Should a `major` (x) bump be inferred?
  - Options considered: (A) no — only minor/patch; (B) infer and suggest major, but never apply without producer approval.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "You can infer it and suggest it, but never implement without checking with the producer." → **Option B**: major may be proposed and justified, gated by the same in-session producer approval as minor.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** – Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (completed)
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** – Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs (completed)
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** – ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (pyproject.toml version source) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: able, acceptance, accepts, access, actual (+331 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: able, acceptance, actual, add, added (+325 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: able, acceptance, accepts, actual, add (+325 more)

# Slot-wait measurement harness counts a read of a fixture file as genuine runs (spurious 999.0 s sample)

Discovered-from: **SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU** (residual post-fix slot-wait re-measurement follow-up).

## Problem statement

The `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` harness's genuine-run filter admits tool results from non-bash tools (e.g. `read`) when their text contains structural markers, so fixture text echoed by a file read is parsed as genuine slot-wait measurements — producing a spurious 999.0 s sample that fails the `no_run_over_120s` threshold.

## Target outcome

Fix the `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` false positive so that reading a fixture/source file can never be counted as a genuine test-slot run, restoring a trustworthy `no_run_over_120s` verdict.

## Users

- **Producer / agent operators** running the slot-wait re-measurement harness to verify the 2026-10-31 fast-lane fix removed test-slot starvation. A false-positive breach invalidates their verdict and blocks RCA closure.
- Example user story: *As a producer closing the slot-starvation RCA (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV), I need the harness verdict to reflect only real runs, so that a `fail` genuinely means users are still waiting > 120 s for a slot.*

## Existing state (evidence, 2026-11-10)

Running `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window reports a spurious **999.0 s** `dev_push_gate` sample. It is an artefact, not a run:

- An agent `read` `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (session record `2026-11-10T15:23:02.987Z`).
- That file contains the fixture text `"slot_wait_seconds": 999.0` plus a `run_tests: gate-subject` marker.
- The harness's genuine-run filter trusts a tool result whose text carries a structural marker when no bash command is resolvable. A `read` tool result has no bash command, so the fixture text is parsed as **four fake gate samples** (122.687, 9.0, 1.25, 999.0).
- Effect: `dev_push_gate` inflates from 5 calls / max 0.002 s to 9 calls / max 999.0 s, and `no_run_over_120s` fails on a non-existent run.

Reproduction (confirmed): `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import measure_slot_wait as m; print(m.parse_block(open('tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py').read())['gate'])"` — prints the four injected samples.

Root cause: `measure()` pairs each `toolResult` with its assistant `toolCall` command via `_commands_by_tool_call`, which maps **only `bash` tool calls**. A `read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep` result therefore resolves to `command=None` and falls through to the `_has_structural_marker` fallback intended for genuine bash runs whose call record is missing (forked/compacted logs).

## Desired change

Distinguish "no command resolvable because the log is incomplete" from "no command because the result came from a non-bash tool". The `toolResult` message itself carries `toolName`; only `bash` results (or a result with no tool name) may use the structural-marker fallback. A result whose `toolName` is a non-bash tool is never a measurement, regardless of its text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `read` (or any non-bash tool) result that merely echoes fixture text is never counted as a genuine run sample.
2. A regression test proves reading `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (and a generic fixture file) injects zero samples.
3. The genuine-run filter still accepts real run sources (`run_tests.py`, `implement.py`, `git push`, `wait_for_job.py`) and genuine structural-marker results with no resolvable command.
4. `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window no longer reports the 999.0 s sample.
5. Testing/validation criterion: the regression test fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The slot-wait re-measurement harness stops reporting phantom breaches, so the parent RCA's threshold verdict is trustworthy.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement tooling; never synthesise load.
- No change to the lane ceilings or threshold values.

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — genuine-run filter in `measure()`; also the module docstring's "Attribution — genuine run filter" section.
- `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — regression test for the fixture-echo false positive.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — "Genuine-run filter" paragraph (needs the bash-only rule stated).

## Related work

- `SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU` — the follow-up item whose re-measurement surfaced this artefact.
- `SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K` — the harness's originating item.
- `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` — parent; its AC3 threshold check is the consumer of this verdict.
- `SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI` — ruff ISC004 flagging `measure_slot_wait.py`; same file, unrelated lint false-positive, do not conflate with this fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the fix must not tighten acceptance for valid cases — genuine structural-marker results from bash runs with missing call records must still pass.
- **Confirmed assumption**: `toolResult` messages carry a `toolName` field set to `"bash"` on genuine bash tool results. Verified across a ~3,000-result sample of `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: `bash` 2346, `read` 394, `edit` 251, `write` 56, `grep` 17, `skill_path` 1 — every genuine run source is `bash`, so a `toolName != "bash"` guard is safe.
- **Assumption**: no non-bash tool legitimately carries slot-wait data in its result text.
- **Scope-creep risk**: do not extend the fix to other measurement harnesses (`measure_audit_performance.py`) unless they exhibit the same pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the work item description provides sufficient evidence, reproduction steps, and acceptance criteria to proceed. Verified independently: (a) the reproduction prints the four injected gate samples; (b) `toolName` is present and `bash`-only for genuine runs across the session corpus; (c) the "Genuine-run filter" docs paragraph is the only prose describing the fallback.
data.title: Slot-wait measurement harness counts a read of a fixture file as genuine runs (spurious 999.0 s sample)

# Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release (`/skill:ship release`) on a contended host, I want the release
gate to distinguish "the suite is red" from "the host is busy", so a busy machine can no longer
fail a green release with a 300 s hang timeout. The unit stage, not a browser loop, was the abort
point this time — the diagnostic currently explains only browser-stage hangs and conflates elapsed
time with the bound.

## Problem statement

A contended host aborts a green unit stage with exit 124 and a diagnostic that (a) describes only
the browser failure mode and (b) prints the **elapsed** time in the sentence that reads as the
**bound**, so an operator cannot tell contention from a genuine hang without opening the cache
entry and re-deriving the numbers by hand.

## Users

- **Release producer** (primary): "When a release aborts in the unit stage I want the log to tell
  me the host was at load 38 on 16 cores and the stage ran 312 s against a 300 s bound, so I retry
  instead of bisecting a green suite."
- **Release producer on an idle host**: "When the unit stage aborts at load 0.4 against a 300 s
  bound, I want the diagnostic to point at a synchronous loop in test/engine code, not at
  `requestAnimationFrame`."
- **CI operator on a small host**: "I want the bound to stay an explicit, overridable number so a
  4-core runner is not handed a bound calibrated for a 16-core workstation."

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The dev→main release gate aborted the TCE v0.1.24 release with
`[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within 300s — aborting (exit 124)` +
`[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=124 outcome=hang args="--project unit" expected=241 ran=indeterminate`.
No test failed — the unit stage was still working through 241 files under host load (three
concurrent suite runs + a Monte-Carlo sweep; 16 cores, load average reported 35–42). A retry cost
a full 20+ minute re-run.

## Existing state (verified in this intake pass, 2026-11-14)

All line numbers verified against the TCE checkout at `main` @ `70b4981f`.

- **The diagnostic takes only the elapsed time.** `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs: number)` at
  `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts:221` builds the line
  `[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within ${elapsedSecs}s` — the bound (`timeoutMs`) is
  never passed in, so the printed number is elapsed wall time wearing the bound's clothes. This is
  the conflation the ACs call out.
- **Two of three hang messages have the defect.** `listHangMessage` (line 237, pre-flight
  `vitest list`) is the same shape; its bound is the constant `LIST_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`
  (line 217). The third message, the coverage-preflight fallback at line 492, already prints the
  *bound* (`Math.round(timeoutMs / 1000)`) — so the codebase is inconsistent rather than uniformly
  wrong, and the fix should unify all three on one shape.
- **Both inputs are already in scope at the call sites.** `runVitestProcess` owns `opts.timeoutMs`
  (the timer at line 1173) and returns `elapsedSecs` (line 1184); the two abort paths
  (`runVitestAsync` line 1214, `runVitestListAsync` line 1246) therefore have bound *and* elapsed
  in hand — the work is threading them into the message plus adding stage and load.
- **Stage is implicit, not first-class.** Nothing in the runner models a stage: `--project unit`
  and `--project browser` are forwarded argv from `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:92` and `:96`. A stage
  value must either be threaded from the caller or derived from the forwarded args, and it must
  cover the pre-flight `vitest list` too (which forwards the same args).
- **The header comment is already stale.** `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:59` says "5 min for unit
  (nominal <2 min)"; the measured worst green unit stage is 217 s — 72 % of the 300 s bound, not
  "<2 min". The rationale cannot be corrected without the measured baseline being recorded beside
  it, which is why the documentation AC is in scope rather than cosmetic.
- **The outer budget has *zero* slack today, not 4–7 min.** `.pi/test-config.json` sets
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500`, applied by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:4551`
  (`args.timeout or suite_timeout_per_command(...) or 600`) to the **single** `npm --silent test`
  command that runs the whole of `run-ci-tests.sh`. Today's stage bounds already sum to
  **300 + 1200 = 1500 s — exactly the outer bound** — and that sum excludes the terminology guard,
  the browser-env pre-check, both `vitest list` pre-flights, the shell orchestration, and the
  (unbounded) Tutorial E2E stage. The 4–7 min of headroom in the original AC is measured against
  the *nominal 18–21 min runtime*, not against the sum of bounds, so it does not cover a raise.
  Any raised or scaled unit bound therefore **must** raise `timeoutPerCommand` in the same change
  (e.g. a 600 s floor ⇒ 1800 s of stage bounds ⇒ outer ≈ 2100–2400 s).
- **An over-budget command is reported separately from a hang.** `run_tests.py` emits the
  `suite_timeout` notice (`NOTICE_SUITE_TIMEOUT`, lines 240 / 3247) — the outer and inner bounds
  must not become confusable in the abort log.
- **The test seam pattern already exists.** `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` (1353
  lines) injects runners, `binPath` and `killGraceMs`; `runVitestProcess` takes an injectable
  `opts` bag. The load average and core count should follow that same injection style.

## Desired change

1. One shared hang-diagnostic builder that always prints **stage, configured bound, elapsed wall
   time, the delta over the bound, host load average at abort and core count** — used by the run
   abort, the pre-flight `vitest list` abort and the coverage-preflight fallback.
2. Stage-appropriate guidance: the `requestAnimationFrame` / undestroyed `Phaser.Game` /
   "run one file under `--project browser`" paragraph is browser-only; a unit-stage abort instead
   points at a synchronous loop in test/engine code. The pre-flight gets the abbreviated form.
3. A unit-stage bound derived as **hybrid**: a raised static floor (justified against the measured
   baseline) plus load-aware scaling from the sampled 1-min load average relative to core count,
   clamped to a finite ceiling, still overridable with `--timeout-ms`.
4. A corrected outer budget (`.pi/test-config.json`) and a corrected rationale in the
   `run-ci-tests.sh` header and the TCE hang-timeout docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (`--project unit` /
  `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound, the elapsed wall time,
  the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the core count — so contention
  is distinguishable from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry. All three hang messages
  (run abort, pre-flight `vitest list` abort, coverage-preflight fallback) share one builder, so the
  current elapsed-as-bound wording at `hangTimeoutMessage`/`listHangMessage` is gone and bound,
  elapsed, stage and load are rendered identically everywhere.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the browser-stage paragraph (starved
  `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`) is
  **not** printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in
  test/engine code.
- The unit-stage wall-clock bound adopts the operator-approved **hybrid** strategy: a raised
  **static floor** (justified against the measured baseline — TCE green unit stages observed at
  88–217 s against the current 300 s bound) **plus load-aware scaling** of the bound from the
  sampled 1-min load average relative to the core count, **up to a finite ceiling**; the bound
  remains overridable per host (`--timeout-ms`), and `--timeout-ms` still wins over the computed
  bound.
- Inner stage bounds stay consistent with the outer gate budget: the sum of stage bounds cannot
  silently exceed the outer per-command timeout — today the bounds already sum to exactly
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` (300 + 1200) with zero slack, so raising or scaling an inner bound
  either adjusts `.pi/test-config.json` in the same change or documents, with the arithmetic, why
  it still fits.
- The hybrid bound's rationale and the measured baseline (88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149,
  206, 217 s) are recorded in the `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` and `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  header comments — replacing the falsified "5 min for unit (nominal <2 min)" — and in the TCE
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout (~line 1313) and the test-config section (~line 816).
- The release gate documents the behaviour on this repo's side: `docs/dev/release-tests.md` gains a
  short "hang abort vs host contention" note stating that a stall is reported as exit 124 with the
  stage/bound/elapsed/load diagnostic, and that a contended-host abort is never auto-retried and
  must be re-run once the host is quiet.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are **never
  retried**, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run; the
  computed bound never exceeds the finite ceiling and never falls below the static floor.
- Tests cover the new diagnostic content (stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average) and the
  bound/load behaviour deterministically: the load average and core count are injected through a
  test seam and are never read from the real host; cases cover an idle host (floor applies), a
  loaded host (scaling applies), and an extreme host (ceiling clamps), plus a browser-stage message
  containing no unit-stage guidance and vice versa.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer can retry a release on a busy machine and see immediately whether the suite or the host
was at fault, instead of losing a full-suite run to a timeout that had nothing to do with the code.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken hang detection.** Exit 124, "hangs are never retried" and the fail-closed
  coverage gate are invariants (TCE precedent CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N, CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H); a bound
  that never fires is a regression in the opposite direction — keep the ceiling finite and print
  the bound in the diagnostic so an operator can see how generous it was.
- **Portability.** The bound must remain an explicit, per-host tunable; a load-aware bound is an
  addition, not a replacement for an overridable number, and smaller CI hosts still get a sane
  floor. `os.loadavg()` is meaningless on Windows — the runner must degrade to the static floor
  there rather than compute a bogus scale.
- **Determinism in tests.** Never read the real load average or core count in a test; sample it
  behind an injectable seam (the `runVitestProcess` `opts` bag / injected-runner pattern already in
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts`).
- **Log noise budget.** The per-attempt `[vitest-runner] ... attempts=N status=S outcome=...` line
  is parsed by release-gate tooling and by `run_tests.py`'s notice classification — the new
  diagnostic enriches the `[hang-timeout]` block and must not break the `[vitest-runner]` line's
  shape.
- **Cross-repo tracking.** This item owns the work; TCE-side files below are edited in the TCE
  checkout (per the cross-repo convention) and recorded on this item. The release gate itself
  lives in `skill/ship/` in this repo.
- **Scope discipline.** A fully load-aware *outer* gate timeout and per-file retry budgets are out
  of scope; record them as linked work items rather than folding them in.
- **Assumption.** Load average at abort is sampled *after* the kill, from the parent runner
  process; it is an indicator of contention during the run, not a measurement integrated over it.
  If a more faithful signal (per-attempt max load) turns out cheap to capture, that is an
  implementation choice for the plan, not a new AC.

## Key Files (predicted)

- **Cross-repo (TCE checkout; tracked here)**
  - `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — `hangTimeoutMessage` (line 221) / `listHangMessage`
    (line 237) / the fallback at line 492 unified into one stage-aware builder; load-average +
    core-count sampling seam; hybrid bound derivation (floor + load scale + ceiling) around
    `DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` (line 188) and `parseRunnerArgs`' `--timeout-ms` (line 322).
  - `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — unit stage `--timeout-ms` (line 92) raised to the new floor;
    header rationale (line ~51–59) corrected against the measured baseline.
  - `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — diagnostic-content assertions and
    floor/scaling/ceiling cases with an injected load average and core count.
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — § Hang timeout (~line 1313) and the test-config section (~line 816).
  - `.pi/test-config.json` — `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` adjusted in the same change as any raised
    unit bound (see the outer-budget AC).
- **This repo (framework)**
  - `docs/dev/release-tests.md` — new "hang abort vs host contention" note (66-line file;
    "How the merge is gated on success" / "Re-running after a fix" are the natural anchors).
  - `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — gate log surface / comments (~line 340–356)
    if the abort is to be surfaced distinctly from a red suite.
  - `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `timeoutPerCommand` handling (line 1488/4551) and the
    `suite_timeout` notice (line 240/3247); read-only unless the outer/inner distinction needs to
    appear in its output.

## Design decision for the plan (not blocking intake)

The hybrid bound may be implemented **in place** in TCE's `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` with
this item tracking the change, or the bounded runner may be **lifted into the framework**
(e.g. under `skill/test/scripts/`) and consumed by TCE. Both satisfy the ACs; the plan decides and
records the choice, keeping the diagnostic and bound computation in exactly one place.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** (TCE, completed) — introduced the bounded wall-clock abort, exit 124,
  the never-retry rule, and raised the browser bound 15→20 min after variance straddled the old
  limit; this item is the same failure mode one stage earlier.
- **CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H** (TCE, completed) — the project-coverage gate whose fail-closed behaviour
  must be preserved.
- **CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09** (TCE, superseded/deleted) — the original intake that produced this
  brief; measured evidence and the evidence corrections (retry log shows a producer-review block,
  not a green retry; load 35–42 is an observation, not a log) carry over.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** (this repo) — the full-suite-at-dev-push gate design this work hardens.
- Sibling item: **SA-0MWEURY420040OMD** (this repo, `intake_complete`) — the green-cache-entry
  resume path; keeps a unit-stage abort from forcing a full re-run of an unchanged tree.
  Complementary, not sequential.
- **SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2** (this repo, completed) — browser-suite contention: two concurrent full
  suites starve each other and vitest runs were SIGKILLed (137) or **hung (124)** at load ~8–12 on
  16 cores. That is the root cause of the collision this item diagnoses; the concurrency ceiling
  change fixed the supply side, this item fixes what the operator is told when it happens anyway
  (three concurrent suites + a Monte-Carlo sweep is not something a semaphore can ration away).
- **SA-0MVXEQSS30045UHL** (this repo, open, `idea`) — the release gate discards the runner JSON, so
  `merge-dev-to-main.sh` cannot say why the suite gate failed (`slot_busy` vs `killed` vs red).
  Same file, adjacent concern, different axis (runner-result consumption, not the hang diagnostic);
  not a blocker either way, but the two touch `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` and
  whichever lands second should rebase its log-surface edit on the other rather than reworking it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (bound strategy: A static raise / B load-aware only / C hybrid) — ANSWERED: C (hybrid).**
  Asked 2026-11-13 by Map in intake on CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09; answered by producer (comment on that
  item): "1. C". Agent recommendation (adopted): C. Research: TCE `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  bounds at lines 56/92/96; `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` and
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` line 816 ("full suite takes 18–21 minutes"); measured green TCE unit stages
  from `.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt` — 88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149, 206, 217 s (worst
  217 s on 2026-11-11 17:37); no load-average awareness exists anywhere in TCE `scripts/` today.
- **Q2 (resume-path scope) — ANSWERED: B (split; framework item).** Answered by producer: "2. B".
  Tracked in the sibling item created alongside this one.
- **Duplicate check** — searched `wl search "hang timeout vitest retry"` (TCE) and this repo's
  items: the browser-stage precedent (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N) is completed and does not cover the
  unit-stage bound, the diagnostics content, or the resume path; no duplicate found.
- **Re-intake verification (2026-11-14, Map, SA-0MWEURUYL004I470) — no new questions asked.** The
  brief was re-verified against the trees rather than re-interviewed; every claim above now carries
  a file:line anchor. Findings that changed the brief: (a) the diagnostic's defect is exactly
  `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs)` printing elapsed time as the bound (`vitest-run-with-retry.ts:221`);
  (b) a third hang message at line 492 already prints the bound, so the fix unifies rather than
  corrects uniformly; (c) the `run-ci-tests.sh:59` rationale "5 min for unit (nominal <2 min)" is
  falsified by the measured 217 s worst green stage; (d) the outer budget has **zero** slack today
  (300 + 1200 = the 1500 s `timeoutPerCommand`), so the original AC's "~4–7 min headroom" was
  measured against nominal runtime and does not cover a raise — the AC now states the arithmetic;
  (e) `os.loadavg()` portability and the `[vitest-runner]` log-shape stability were added as
  constraints; (f) `docs/dev/release-tests.md` named as the framework-side documentation target.
  Issue type (`feature`) and priority (`high`) re-confirmed; no operator input required.
## Plan (2026-11-14, Map — `/skill:plan`)

**Effort:** Medium (PERT expected 48.7 h, recommended 70.7 h) · **Risk:** Medium (score 11/25,
probability 2.1 × impact 5) · **Approval gate:** not requested (the gate requests approval only
for Extra Large **and** High/Severe). Six children, test/verification first in creation order.

### Design decisions the plan owns

- **D1 — Implementation stays in place in TCE.** The bounded runner remains
  `Tableau-Card-Engine: scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, tracked by this item. Rationale: the
  runner is a Node/TS module invoked by TCE's `npm test` and inherited by consuming game repos
  through their TCE pin, its 1353-line test suite lives beside it, and the framework has no TS
  distribution path for `skill/` scripts. Lifting it into `skill/test/` would need a new
  cross-repo packaging mechanism and would split the runner from its tests, for no gain. The
  diagnostic **and** the bound computation therefore live in exactly one file.
- **D2 — `--timeout-ms` remains a strict, verbatim override** (parent AC3: "`--timeout-ms` still
  wins"). Consequence: the shell must stop pinning the unit bound, otherwise the hybrid bound can
  never apply. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` therefore **drops** `--timeout-ms 300000` from the unit
  stage (the runner's hybrid bound applies) and **keeps** the explicit browser bound
  (`--timeout-ms 1200000`). This intentionally differs from the Key Files hint "unit stage
  `--timeout-ms` raised to the new floor" — a pinned unit bound and load-aware scaling cannot
  both hold; the floor is expressed as the runner constant instead.
- **D3 — Hybrid bound formula.** Static floor **600 s** (2.8× the worst measured green unit stage
  of 217 s, 2× the old 300 s bound); finite ceiling **1200 s** (equal to the browser bound);
  scaling `factor = clamp((load1m / cpuCount) / 0.75, 1, 2)` so `bound = clamp(600 s × factor,
  600 s, 1200 s)` — the floor applies at ≤0.75 load/core, the ceiling at ≥1.5 load/core (e.g. 24
  load on 16 cores). Load is sampled **before** the stage starts (to size the bound) and **at
  abort** (for the diagnostic, per the intake assumption), through one injected seam; on Windows
  the load is unavailable and the floor applies.
- **D4 — Outer budget.** Worst case = unit 1200 + browser 1200 + two `vitest list` pre-flights
  240 + terminology/env pre-checks and orchestration ≈ 60 ⇒ **`.pi/test-config.json`
  `timeoutPerCommand: 2700`** (was 1500, which already had zero slack). Accepted trade-off: a
  genuine hang can now take up to ~45 min to abort instead of ~25 min — the deliberate price of
  not aborting green stages on a contended host, and the diagnostic prints the bound so the
  generosity is visible. (A 900 s ceiling with `timeoutPerCommand: 2400` was the smaller-footprint
  alternative; rejected because 900 s is only 4.1× the worst measured stage and the incident ran
  under sustained load ≥2/core.)
- **D5 — Log shape is frozen.** The `[hang-timeout]` block is enriched; the
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=N status=S outcome=…` line and the `suite_timeout` notice keep their
  exact shape (release-gate tooling and `run_tests.py` notice classification parse them).
- **D6 — `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` is not touched.** Its log surface is
  owned by SA-0MVXEQSS30045UHL (runner JSON discarded); this item only documents the gate
  behaviour in `docs/dev/release-tests.md`.

### Feature breakdown (creation order = test-first order)

| # | Child | Type | Slice | Parent ACs |
| - | ----- | ---- | ----- | ---------- |
| 1 | Verify hang diagnostics and gate budget (SA-0MWFX7VVX002HF1Q) | task | verification (runs last) | AC7, AC8, AC10 |
| 2 | Injectable host contention sampler seam (SA-0MWFX7ZFO009YE0Y) | task | test-first seam | AC1/AC3 inputs, AC8 |
| 3 | Stage-aware unified hang diagnostic builder (SA-0MWFX836K006QWEH) | feature | diagnostic end-to-end | AC1, AC2 |
| 4 | Hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound (SA-0MWFX86ZY0000WVR) | feature | bound end-to-end | AC3, AC7 |
| 5 | Unit bound wiring and outer gate budget (SA-0MWFX8A7I00883VQ) | feature | shell wiring + budget | AC4, AC5 |
| 6 | Document hang baseline, rationale and contention (SA-0MWFX8D8X007PH6Y) | docs | TCE + framework + wiki docs | AC5, AC6, AC9 |

**Parent AC legend** (in description order): AC1 diagnostic content + single builder · AC2
stage-appropriate guidance · AC3 hybrid bound (floor + scaling + ceiling, override wins) · AC4
inner bounds consistent with the outer budget · AC5 rationale + baseline in code headers and TCE
docs · AC6 framework `docs/dev/release-tests.md` note · AC7 hang semantics unchanged · AC8
deterministic tests with injected load/cores · AC9 all related docs · AC10 full suite green.

### Sequencing and vertical slices

Each implementation child is a vertical slice (code + tests + its own header/doc comment), not a
horizontal layer: the sampler seam lands first with its tests, then the diagnostic slice, then
the bound slice, then the wiring/budget slice, then the documentation slice, then the
cross-cutting verification. Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update it if
the previous slice changed a name or a number (e.g. the derivation's signature, the final
`timeoutPerCommand`).

**Cross-repo:** children 2–6 edit the TCE checkout (`~/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine`, prefix
`CG`) on a `dev`-based branch — commit messages name this item (`SA-0MWEURUYL004I470`) and the
hash is recorded here; child 6 also edits `docs/dev/release-tests.md` in this repo.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-14 — Initial decomposition (6 children, 8 dependency edges), design decisions D1–D6,
  effort/risk estimate (Medium/Medium at intake stage) and AC→child traceability recorded.

- **Planning session (2026-11-14, Map, `/skill:plan`) — no new producer questions asked.** The
  intake brief already carried a verified existing state (file:line anchors) and the producer's
  Q1 = C (hybrid) answer, and it explicitly delegated the in-place-vs-lift design decision to the
  plan, so planning recorded decisions D1–D6 instead of re-interviewing. Notable resolution: the
  brief's Key Files hint "unit stage `--timeout-ms` raised to the new floor" is **not**
  implementable alongside AC3's "`--timeout-ms` still wins" — a pinned unit bound makes the
  load-aware scaling inert — so D2 drops the unit pin in `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` and expresses
  the floor as a runner constant. Concrete numbers chosen against the measured baseline: floor
  600 s, ceiling 1200 s, scaling `clamp((load1m/cores)/0.75, 1, 2)`, `timeoutPerCommand` 1500 →
  2700. Effort/risk: Medium / Medium (PERT expected 49.6 h, recommended 71.6 h; risk score
  10/25) — below the approval gate (Extra Large **and** High/Severe), so no approval pause was
  raised.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MWEURY420040OMD** – Release gate: preserve green full-suite cache entries so a hang abort resumes (in-progress)
- **SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2** – Browser suite contention: TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 lets two full suites starve each other (137 kills / 124 hangs) (completed)
- **SA-0MVXEQSS30045UHL** – Release gate (merge-dev-to-main.sh) discards the runner JSON, so a dev→main release cannot say why the suite gate failed (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, 300s, abort, aborted, aborting (+288 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, abort, aborted, aborting, acceptance (+278 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, 300s, abort, aborted, aborting (+270 more)

# Verify: hang diagnostics and gate budget (test/verification slice)

**Parent:** SA-0MWEURUYL004I470 — Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound
**Slice type:** verification (created before the implementation children; runs last, gated on them)
**Parent ACs covered:** AC8 (deterministic diagnostic/bound tests), AC7 (hang semantics unchanged), AC10 (full suite passes)

## Goal

As the release producer, I want proof that the new `[hang-timeout]` diagnostic and the
hybrid bound actually behave as documented — on an idle host, a loaded host and at the
ceiling — and that the release gate's bounds still fit its outer budget — so I trust the
gate after the change instead of discovering a regression in the next release.

## Scope

Cross-cutting verification of the work delivered by the sibling children. This item adds or
completes assertions only where a sibling's tests leave a hole; it does not re-implement
their tests (see `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — no duplicate core coverage).

## Minimal implementation

- Run the full TCE suite with the new bounds and record the outcome (green) plus the observed
  unit/browser stage wall times from the run log.
- Recompute and record the budget arithmetic: unit ceiling + browser bound + both `vitest list`
  pre-flight bounds + pre-check/orchestration overhead vs `.pi/test-config.json`
  `timeoutPerCommand`.
- Exercise the abort path with a fake vitest binary (the existing `writeFakeBin` helper in
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts`) and capture the rendered `[hang-timeout]`
  block for the run stage, the `vitest list` pre-flight and (by injection) the coverage
  pre-flight fallback; assert stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load and cores are all present and
  that the `[vitest-runner] attempts=N status=S outcome=hang …` line shape is unchanged.
- Confirm the never-retry and fail-closed coverage invariants with the existing tests plus one
  end-to-end assertion that a hang still exits 124.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests cover the new diagnostic content (stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average) and the bound/load behaviour deterministically: the load average and core count are injected through a test seam and are never read from the real host; cases cover an idle host (floor applies), a loaded host (scaling applies), and an extreme host (ceiling clamps), plus a browser-stage message containing no unit-stage guidance and vice versa.
- Hang semantics are confirmed unchanged by executed tests: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are never retried, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run; the computed bound never exceeds the finite ceiling and never falls below the static floor.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- The recorded arithmetic shows the sum of worst-case stage bounds (unit ceiling + browser bound + both `vitest list` pre-flight bounds + orchestration overhead) is strictly below `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand`.
- A captured abort transcript for each of the three hang messages shows stage, configured bound, elapsed wall time, delta over the bound, load average and core count rendered identically, with the `[vitest-runner]` line shape unchanged.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — end-to-end abort assertions and the fake-bin helper.
- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — read-only reference for the rendered block.
- `.pi/test-config.json` — the outer budget value being verified.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — the stage bounds being summed.

## Dependencies

Blocked by all implementation children: sampler seam, diagnostic builder, hybrid bound,
bound wiring/outer budget, and documentation (the docs assert the numbers this item verifies).

## Definition of done

- Every AC above is met and evidenced on this item (run log path, captured transcript, arithmetic).
- Full TCE suite green; `[vitest-runner]` line shape unchanged.
- TCE commit hash + message and the framework commit hash (if any) recorded on this item.

# Stage-aware unified hang diagnostic builder

**Parent:** SA-0MWEURUYL004I470 — Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound
**Slice type:** feature (tracer bullet: diagnostic end-to-end — code, tests, header comment)
**Parent ACs covered:** AC1, AC2

## Goal

As a release producer whose gate aborted in the unit stage, I want one `[hang-timeout]` block
that tells me the stage, the configured bound, the elapsed time, how far over the bound the
stage ran and what the host load was — with guidance written for the stage that actually
aborted — so I can tell contention from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry.

## Context (verified 2026-11-14, TCE `main` @ `70b4981f`)

- `hangTimeoutMessage(elapsedSecs: number)` (`scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts:221`) and
  `listHangMessage(elapsedSecs: number)` (`:237`) print **elapsed** time in the sentence that
  reads as the **bound**; the coverage-preflight fallback (`:492`) already prints the bound.
  Three messages, two shapes, one conflation to remove.
- Both inputs are already in scope at the abort sites: `runVitestProcess` owns `opts.timeoutMs`
  and returns `elapsedSecs`; `runVitestAsync` (`:1214`) and `runVitestListAsync` (`:1246`)
  therefore have bound and elapsed in hand.
- Stage is implicit: `--project unit` / `--project browser` arrive as forwarded argv from
  `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:92` and `:96`; the pre-flight forwards the same args.
- The browser guidance (`requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under
  `--project browser`) is currently printed for **every** hang, including unit-stage aborts.

## Minimal implementation

- Add one exported `hangDiagnostic(context)` builder taking
  `{ stage, boundMs, elapsedSecs, contention }` and rendering the single shared shape:
  `[hang-timeout] <stage> did not complete within <bound>s — aborting (exit 124)`,
  then `elapsed <n>s (+<delta>s over bound)`, then `host load <l> over <cores> cores`.
- Derive the stage from the forwarded args (`--project <name>`, else `unknown project`); label
  the pre-flight `vitest list (<args>)`. One derivation helper, used by both abort paths.
- Route `runVitestAsync`, `runVitestListAsync` and the coverage-preflight fallback in
  `deriveExpectedFiles` through the builder; drop the `elapsedSecs`-only signatures (no
  backwards-compatible alias — this is an internal script).
- Select guidance by stage: browser block unchanged; unit block points at a synchronous loop in
  test/engine code (`testTimeout` cannot preempt synchronous JS — attach the V8 inspector per
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md`); pre-flight gets the abbreviated form.
- Write the assertions first (rendered content + stage selection), then implement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (`--project unit` / `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound, the elapsed wall time, the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the core count — so contention is distinguishable from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry. All three hang messages (run abort, pre-flight `vitest list` abort, coverage-preflight fallback) share one builder, so the current elapsed-as-bound wording at `hangTimeoutMessage`/`listHangMessage` is gone and bound, elapsed, stage and load are rendered identically everywhere.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the browser-stage paragraph (starved `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`) is **not** printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in test/engine code.
- The stage label is derived once from the forwarded args and is correct for `--project unit`, `--project browser`, an unrecognised project (rendered as the raw project name, never blank) and the pre-flight `vitest list` path.
- Tests assert the rendered block contains the stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average and core count, that a browser block contains the `requestAnimationFrame` guidance and a unit block does not (and vice versa), and that no rendered number is labelled as the bound when it is the elapsed time.
- Exit code semantics are untouched: the block still reports exit `124` and still states that no retry is performed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — builder, stage derivation, the two abort paths, the coverage-preflight fallback.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — rendered-content, stage-selection and guidance assertions (extend the existing `hang timeout (bounded wall-clock abort)` block).
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — read-only: confirms the forwarded `--project` args are the stage source.

## Dependencies

- Injectable host contention sampler seam (load average + core count for the block).

## Definition of done

- Tests written first; changed-scope test gate green.
- The `[vitest-runner] attempts=N status=S outcome=hang …` line shape is unchanged.
- ACs evidenced on this item; TCE commit hash + message recorded here.

# Hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound

**Parent:** SA-0MWEURUYL004I470 — Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound
**Slice type:** feature (tracer bullet: bound derivation end-to-end — code, tests, header comment)
**Parent ACs covered:** AC3, AC7

## Goal

As a release producer on a contended host, I want the unit stage's wall-clock bound to grow
with the load the host is actually carrying — from a raised floor up to a finite ceiling — so a
busy machine no longer aborts a green suite at a bound calibrated for an idle one, while a true
hang is still bounded.

## Context (verified 2026-11-14, TCE `main` @ `70b4981f`)

- `DEFAULT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 min` (`scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts:188`);
  `parseRunnerArgs` parses `--timeout-ms` at `:322` and it today always wins.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh:92` currently pins the unit bound at `--timeout-ms 300000`, so any
  computed bound would be inert unless the shell stops pinning it (see the wiring child).
- Measured green unit stages: 88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149, 206, 217 s (worst 217 s =
  72 % of the 300 s bound, 2026-11-11 17:37).
- No load-average awareness exists anywhere in TCE `scripts/` today; `node:os` is already
  imported in the runner.

## Design (decided by this plan; the producer picked "hybrid" at intake, Q1 = C)

- **Static floor** `UNIT_FLOOR_MS = 600_000` (600 s): 2.8× the worst measured green unit stage
  (217 s) and 2× the previous 300 s bound — enough headroom that a merely busy host still
  completes, while a genuinely stuck stage is still aborted.
- **Finite ceiling** `UNIT_CEILING_MS = 1_200_000` (1200 s): equal to the browser bound, and the
  value the outer gate budget is sized against.
- **Load-aware scaling**: `perCore = load1m / cpuCount`;
  `factor = clamp(perCore / 0.75, 1, 2)`; `bound = clamp(floor × factor, floor, ceiling)`.
  At ≤0.75 load/core the floor applies (600 s); at ≥1.5 load/core the ceiling applies
  (1200 s) — e.g. 24 on 16 cores.
- **Override wins verbatim**: an explicit `--timeout-ms` is used as-is with no scaling
  (AC3's "`--timeout-ms` still wins"), so a 4-core CI runner can pin its own number.
- **Portability**: when the sampler reports the load as unavailable (Windows), the floor applies.
- The derivation is a pure exported function so it is testable without spawning anything.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the pure `deriveUnitBound({ floorMs, ceilingMs, load1m, cpuCount, overrideMs })` (name may
  vary) plus the two constants, documented in the file header against the measured baseline.
- Wire it into `parseRunnerArgs`/`main`: absent `--timeout-ms` ⇒ computed bound for `--project
  unit`; explicit `--timeout-ms` ⇒ verbatim. Keep the browser stage's default behaviour as-is
  (no load scaling) so this change is unit-stage-only.
- Pass the same contention sample to the diagnostic so the printed bound is the bound actually
  enforced.
- Write the boundary tests first (idle / loaded / extreme / override / unavailable load), then
  implement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The unit-stage wall-clock bound adopts the operator-approved hybrid strategy: a raised static floor (600 s, justified against the measured baseline — TCE green unit stages observed at 88–217 s against the current 300 s bound) plus load-aware scaling of the bound from the sampled 1-min load average relative to the core count, up to a finite ceiling (1200 s); the bound remains overridable per host (`--timeout-ms`), and `--timeout-ms` still wins over the computed bound.
- The bound derivation is a pure, exported function with the floor and ceiling as explicit constants, so an operator can see the numbers without running a suite; the computed bound never exceeds the finite ceiling and never falls below the static floor for any load value, core count or override.
- Tests cover an idle host (floor applies), a loaded host (scaling applies between floor and ceiling) and an extreme host (ceiling clamps), plus `--timeout-ms` overrides winning verbatim and an unavailable load average (Windows) falling back to the floor; the load average and core count are injected through the test seam and never read from the real host.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are never retried, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run; a bound that cannot fire is not acceptable, so the ceiling is finite and printed in the diagnostic.
- The browser stage's existing bound behaviour is unchanged — the load-aware derivation applies to the unit stage only.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — constants, pure derivation, `parseRunnerArgs`/`main` wiring, header rationale.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — floor/scaling/ceiling/override/unavailable-load cases with injected inputs.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — read-only here; the wiring child changes the invocation.

## Dependencies

- Injectable host contention sampler seam.

## Definition of done

- Boundary tests written first; changed-scope test gate green.
- ACs evidenced on this item; TCE commit hash + message recorded here.
